_readme: Hand-maintained inputs for scripts/gen-config-reference.mjs. The JSON schema in the product repo is the structural source of truth (keys, types, enums, min/max).
The schema omits many defaults and descriptions, so this file supplies them. Every value here was read from the C# options classes of the release named in _verifiedAgainst.
Each entry has a 'source' that names the file to re-read at the next release. When a default in C# changes, edit it here and re-run the script.
keys:    overrides for keys that exist in the schema (default, description, type, allowed). An override for a key that has left the schema fails the run.
shared:  overrides applied to each prefix in 'prefixes' (the three chat channels). An explicit entry in 'keys' wins.
extra:   keys the daemon reads that the schema does not list (chat channel secrets, MCP client secret). 'after' pins the row position.
sections: one-paragraph orientation per top-level key, rendered above each table. 'notes' renders below it.
skip:    schema paths that are not rendered as rows.

Enabled.description: Start this channel adapter. Needs the bot token in `secrets.json`.

DefaultChannelId.description: Default channel for messages the bot starts itself, such as reminder deliveries. It also counts as an allowed channel.

MentionOnly.description: Respond in channels only when the bot is mentioned.

AllowDirectMessages.description: Accept direct messages. DMs use the audience mapped to the `dm` key in `ChannelAudiences`.

MentionRequiredInDm.description: Require a mention in DMs too. Applies only when `AllowDirectMessages` is `true`.

MentionRequiredInThreadByChannel.description: Per-channel switch, keyed by channel ID. `true` requires a mention in thread replies even when the thread already has an active session. A channel with no entry doesn't.

AllowedChannelIds.description: Channel IDs the bot responds in, in addition to `DefaultChannelId`. Messages from any other channel are denied.

AllowedUserIds.description: User IDs allowed to talk to the bot. An empty list allows every user in an allowed channel. A listed user is treated as a trusted internal principal.

ChannelAudiences.description: Audience per channel, keyed by channel ID or `dm`. Unmapped channels fall back to the ACL heuristic. The audience picks the `Tools.AudienceProfiles` entry that applies.

Slack.SocketMode.description: Connect over Slack Socket Mode. Needs the app-level token (`Slack.AppToken`).

Slack.DefaultChannelName.description: A channel name the daemon resolves to an ID at startup when `DefaultChannelId` is unset. An unresolved name logs a warning. The `netclaw config` Slack editor deletes it and writes the ID.

Logging.LogLevel.Default.description: Minimum level written to `daemon-<date>.log`. An unset or unrecognized value gives `Information`. Other keys under `Logging.LogLevel` (for example `Microsoft`) set per-category levels.

Logging.Console.Enabled.description: Also write single-line log output to the console. Docker and systemd capture it.

Telemetry.Enabled.description: Export metrics and logs over OTLP. netclaw has no tracing exporter.

Telemetry.Otlp.Endpoint.description: OTLP collector base URL. Must be an absolute URI. Over HTTP/protobuf netclaw posts to `v1/logs` and `v1/metrics` under it, and reduces a full signal URL to its base. gRPC uses the URL unchanged.

Session.MemoryObserverIdleSeconds.description: Seconds of quiet before the memory observer distills the conversation into memories.

Session.IdleTimeout.description: How long a session sits idle before it saves a snapshot and passivates. Format `HH:mm:ss`. `00:00:00` disables passivation. Background jobs owned by the session are killed when it passivates.

Session.TurnLlmTimeoutSeconds.description: Timeout for the main per-turn model call. Also feeds the `FirstTokenTimeoutSeconds` fallback.

Session.ToolExecutionTimeoutSeconds.description: Inactivity budget per tool call. The call must produce its first result within this time and each later streamed item resets it. A stuck tool fails alone without affecting the others in the batch. Background shell jobs aren't bound by it.

Session.SidecarLlmTimeoutSeconds.description: Timeout for background model calls: title generation, memory distillation and compaction notes. Raise it for slow models.

Memory.Curation.NominatorSimilarityThres.description: Embedding cosine similarity threshold above which an existing memory is nominated for the curation call to adjudicate.

Session.FirstTokenTimeoutSeconds.description: Maximum silence between streamed deltas once the first one arrives. Subagent runs use it too, since agent definitions no longer carry `timeoutSeconds`. If unset, it uses `TurnLlmTimeoutSeconds` when you changed that, otherwise 600.

Session.PrefillTimeoutSeconds.description: Maximum wait for the first streamed delta. Covers queue wait and prompt prefill, which can take minutes on self-hosted backends.

Session.NoProgressTimeoutSeconds.description: Hard ceiling on time without a real output token. Keepalive heartbeats don't reset it, so a backend that heartbeats forever without producing a token is killed when it elapses. The value also sets the thinking cap: one model call that streams only thinking, with no answer text and no tool call, stops at three times this value.

Session.MaxToolIterationsPerTurn.description: Legacy key kept so existing files still load. It is validated (1 to 500) but no longer limits a turn. netclaw refuses a call that repeats the same work, and the watchdog timeouts bound the rest.

Session.CompactionThreshold.description: Fraction of the context window that triggers compaction. Same as `Session.Tuning.CompactionThreshold`. The `Tuning` value wins when both are set.

Session.SnapshotInterval.description: Turns between persistence snapshots. Same as `Session.Tuning.SnapshotInterval`.

Session.KeepRecentToolResults.description: Recent tool call and result pairs kept in full when compaction clears older results. Same as `Session.Tuning.KeepRecentToolResults`.

Session.MaxInlineToolResultChars.description: Largest tool result placed inline in the conversation. For longer output the last this-many characters stay inline, the rest is dropped from the inline text, and the full output goes to a session file the model reads with `tool_output_read`. `shell_execute` has its own smaller budget of 2,000. Same as `Session.Tuning.MaxInlineToolResultChars`.

Session.DiscoveredToolRetentionTurns.description: User turns a tool loaded with `load_tool` stays available. `0` makes the model load it again every turn. Same as `Session.Tuning.DiscoveredToolRetentionTurns`.

Session.DiscoveredToolMaxCount.description: Most loaded deferred or MCP tools kept across turns. The oldest are evicted first. Same as `Session.Tuning.DiscoveredToolMaxCount`.

Session.KeepRecentMessages.description: Recent messages kept verbatim after compaction summarizes the rest. Counts raw messages, not turn pairs. Same as `Session.Tuning.KeepRecentMessages`.

Session.TitleGenerationInterval.description: Turns between session title refreshes. The title is always generated on turn 1. `0` disables refreshes. Same as `Session.Tuning.TitleGenerationInterval`.

Session.DeterministicRetrievalEnabled.description: Plan automatic memory recall deterministically on each turn. Scheduled for removal, leave it on. Same as `Session.Tuning.DeterministicRetrievalEnabled`.

Session.Tuning.description: Internal tuning. Every key here has a same-named key directly under `Session`, and the `Tuning` value wins.

Session.Tuning.MemoryDistillationTurnInt.description: Completed turns between memory distillation passes, regardless of idle state, so memories form during long active sessions. `0` leaves distillation to `MemoryObserverIdleSeconds`.

Session.Tuning.MinimumRecallCompositeSco.description: Minimum composite score for a memory to be injected by automatic recall. Unset uses the coordinator's built-in floor. Lower values let weaker matches through, `0` removes the floor.

Session.Tuning.MaxRecallInjectedChars.description: Character budget for memory text injected by automatic recall in one turn. Whole items are dropped rather than truncated. `0` removes the budget.

Security.DeploymentPosture.description: Who talks to this install: `Personal` (you), `Team` or `Public`. `netclaw init` writes it. When it's unset and `StrictDefaults` is `true`, netclaw behaves as `Public` and denies `shell_execute`. It selects the default tool profiles and shell mode, and it narrows the audience of every turn: a channel mapped to `Personal` under a `Team` posture runs as `Team`.

Security.ShellExecutionMode.description: Whether `shell_execute` can run. Unset gives `HostAllowed` for a `Personal` posture and `Off` for the others. `Tools.ShellMode` overrides it. `SandboxOnly` denies every shell call with `shell_requires_sandbox_backend`.

Security.StrictDefaults.description: Fail closed when posture or shell mode is unset. Set `false` only to get `Personal` and `HostAllowed` as the implicit defaults.

Tools.ShellMode.description: Overrides `Security.ShellExecutionMode` for the shell tools. Unset follows the security setting.

Tools.MaxOutputChars.description: Most output a tool call captures in memory for the spill file. It isn't what the model sees inline, which is `Session.MaxInlineToolResultChars`. Output past the ceiling is discarded.

Tools.AudienceProfiles.description: Per-audience tool, file and MCP grants. Public, Team and Personal share one shape. A list you set replaces the default list and doesn't merge with it.

Tools.AudienceProfiles.<audience>.ToolsM.description: `Allowlist` grants only the tools in `AllowedTools`. `All` grants every profile-managed tool.

Tools.AudienceProfiles.<audience>.Allowe.description: Profile-managed tools this audience can call. Tools outside the profile-managed set are always available. Setting the key replaces the default list, and a value that isn't a list stops startup.

Tools.AudienceProfiles.<audience>.McpSer.description: `Allowlist` exposes only the servers in `AllowedMcpServers`. `All` exposes every configured server.

Tools.AudienceProfiles.<audience>.Allowe.description: MCP server names this audience can use when `McpServersMode` is `Allowlist`. MCP stays off for Public and Team until you add a server.

Tools.AudienceProfiles.<audience>.McpSer.description: Per-server tool allowlists. A server listed here exposes only the named tools. A server not listed exposes all of its tools. Ignored when `McpServersMode` is `All`.

Tools.AudienceProfiles.<audience>.ReadFi.description: `None` blocks it, `Roots` limits it to `Roots`, `All` allows any path that isn't protected. For the `Personal` audience, `file_read`, `file_list`, `file_search` and `attach_file` reach at least as far as `WriteFiles` does.

Tools.AudienceProfiles.<audience>.WriteF.description: Directories used when `Mode` is `Roots`. Same tokens as `ReadFiles.Roots`.

Tools.AudienceProfiles.<audience>.Attach.description: Directories used when `Mode` is `Roots`. Same tokens as `ReadFiles.Roots`.

Tools.AudienceProfiles.<audience>.Approv.description: Which tools need a human to approve each call. See [How tool approvals work](/security/approvals/).
Mode for tools with no override.

Mode per tool. Keys are tool names (`shell_execute`) or MCP tools as `server/tool` (or `server__tool`), matched without regard to case. If two keys differ only by case, the more restrictive mode wins. A key that contains `:` or has no value is ignored, so the tool keeps the audience default, and `netclaw doctor` reports it. Writes to the config directory are denied before any approval mode is read.

Mode for every tool of one MCP server, keyed by server name and matched without regard to case. An exact `ToolOverrides` entry wins. A key that contains `:` is ignored and `netclaw doctor` reports it.

Tools.AudienceProfiles.<audience>.Channe.description: Which files from chat messages this audience can send in.
Attachment categories accepted. An empty list rejects every attachment.
Largest file accepted, in bytes (25 MiB). Must be above 0 when any category is allowed.
Most files accepted on one message. A message over the limit loses all its attachments. Must be above 0 when any category is allowed.

Tools.AudienceProfiles.GlobalReadRoots.description: Directories every audience can read, so skill loading, identity files and project discovery work under Team and Public. Setting the key replaces the list.

Tools.WebFetch.RequireHttps.description: Reject plain `http://` URLs in `web_fetch` unless the host is in `HttpAllowList`.

Tools.WebFetch.HttpAllowList.description: Hosts that may use plain HTTP when `RequireHttps` is `true`. Setting the key replaces the list, so keep the loopback entries if you still need them.

Tools.HardDenyPatterns.description: Extra shell verb-chain prefixes that are always blocked and can't be approved. They add to the built-in hard-deny list, they don't replace it.

Providers.description: LLM provider connections keyed by a name you choose. `Models.Definitions` entries refer to these names.

Models.Definitions.description: Model definitions keyed by a name you choose, at least one. Names are case-insensitive and must be unique.

Models.Definitions.<name>.description: One model: which provider serves it and how it behaves.

Models.Definitions.<name>.ModelId.description: Model identifier sent to the provider.

Models.Definitions.<name>.ContextWindow.description: Context window in tokens. When set, it caps the value the provider reports.

Models.Definitions.<name>.Provenance.description: Where the model data came from: `Live`, `Defaults` or `Manual`. netclaw sets it. You don't need to.

Models.Definitions.<name>.InputModalitie.description: Manual override for what the model accepts, comma-separated from `Text`, `Image`, `Audio`, `Video`. Turns off automatic detection.

Models.Definitions.<name>.OutputModaliti.description: Manual override for what the model produces. Same format as `InputModalities`.

Models.Definitions.<name>.MaxOutputToken.description: Output limit in tokens for every call of this model. Thinking tokens count inside it. Must be below `ContextWindow` when that is set. Unset sends 32000, clamped per call to the model maximum and to the context window minus the estimated prompt.

Models.Definitions.<name>.Thinking.description: Provider-neutral thinking level for every call of this model. `Max` is the highest level the provider offers. A level the provider dialect can't send fails startup. Unset uses the model's default.

Models.Roles.description: Which definition plays each role. Values are names from `Definitions`.

Models.Roles.Fallback.description: Failover model. Falls back to `Main` when unset.

Models.Roles.Compaction.description: Cheaper or faster model for compaction. Falls back to `Main` when unset.

Memory.Recall.MinCosineSimilarity.default: unset (follows the model, 0.24 for the default)
Memory.Recall.MinCosineSimilarity.description: Cosine floor for automatic recall. Candidates below it are dropped before ranking. The meaning is specific to the active embedding model, so recalibrate before you set it.

Memory.Recall.RelevanceGate.Enabled.description: Run the cross-encoder relevance gate on recall candidates. Set it explicitly to turn the gate on or off independently of embeddings.

Memory.Recall.RelevanceGate.Threshold.description: Score below which the gate drops a candidate. Unset uses the calibrated value for the provisioned relevance model.

ExternalSkills.Sources.description: Ordered list of external skill sources. Earlier entries win name collisions and native netclaw skills always win.

ExternalSkills.Sources[].Name.description: Unique name for the source, for example `claude-code`.

SkillFeeds.Feeds.description: Ordered list of skill server feeds. Earlier feeds win name collisions.

SkillFeeds.Feeds[].Name.description: Unique feed name, lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. Used as the directory name.

Notifications.Webhooks.description: Targets that receive operational alerts by HTTP POST. Empty means alerts only go to the log.

Notifications.Webhooks[].Url.description: HTTP or HTTPS endpoint to POST alerts to.

Notifications.Webhooks[].Headers.description: Static headers sent with every POST, for example `Authorization`.

Webhooks.Enabled.description: Register the inbound webhook endpoint and the `set_webhook`, `list_webhooks` and `delete_webhook` tools.

Webhooks.ExecutionTimeoutSeconds.description: Longest a webhook-triggered run can take before the daemon marks it failed.

Workspaces.Directory.description: Root for project workspaces. Projects are Git repositories with an `AGENTS.md`, at any depth. A leading `~` expands to your home directory.

McpServers.<server>.Transport.description: How netclaw connects: `stdio` runs `Command`, `sse` and `http` connect to `Url`.

McpServers.<server>.EnvironmentVariables.description: Environment variables passed to the `stdio` process. Values stored in `secrets.json` are decrypted first.

McpServers.<server>.Headers.description: HTTP headers for `sse` and `http`. Values stored in `secrets.json` are decrypted first.

McpServers.<server>.Enabled.description: Disabled servers are skipped at startup.

McpServers.<server>.GrantCategory.description: Tool metadata category for the server's tools. Authorization doesn't read it: use the audience's `AllowedMcpServers` and `McpServerToolGrants`.

McpServers.<server>.OAuthClientId.description: Static OAuth client ID for servers without dynamic client registration.

McpServers.<server>.OAuthScope.description: Space-separated OAuth scopes to request, overriding the server's defaults.

Search.BraveApiKey.description: Brave Search API token. Required when `Backend` is `brave`. Lives in `secrets.json`: `netclaw secrets set Search.BraveApiKey <token>`.

Search.SearXngEndpoint.description: SearXNG instance base URL, for example `http://searxng.local:8080`. Required when `Backend` is `searxng`.

Memory.Embeddings.description: Local ONNX embedding model for semantic memory.

Memory.Curation.description: How new memories are checked against existing ones before they're saved.

Memory.Recall.description: How automatic recall ranks and filters memories, mixing keyword and vector scores.

Memory.Embeddings.ModelId.description: Embedding model to use. Allowed ids are `snowflake-arctic-embed-m-int8`, `snowflake-arctic-embed-m` and `mxbai-embed-large-v1`. An id outside the allowlist is a configuration error. Changing it re-embeds existing memories under the new id.

SubAgents.PrefillTimeoutSeconds.description: Longest wait for a subagent's first streamed token, which covers queue wait and prompt prefill. Same idea as `Session.PrefillTimeoutSeconds`. After the first token the `Session.FirstTokenTimeoutSeconds` budget applies. An agent definition can override it with `prefillTimeoutSeconds` in its frontmatter.

SubAgents.NoProgressTimeoutSeconds.description: Hard ceiling on a subagent run with no real output token. Keepalives don't reset it. Like `Session.NoProgressTimeoutSeconds`, it also sets the thinking cap at three times the value.

Daemon.UpdateChannel.description: Release channel the update check follows. `stable` only sees stable releases. `beta` also sees prereleases and moves to a stable release once one supersedes the beta.

Notifications.Webhooks[].Format.description: Payload format: `Generic` is a JSON envelope, `Slack` is Slack Block Kit.

Mattermost.ServerUrl.description: Base URL of the Mattermost server, for example `https://mm.example.com`.

Mattermost.CallbackUrl.description: URL Mattermost can reach for interactive button callbacks, for example `http://netclaw-host:5199/api/mattermost/actions`. When unset, approvals fall back to text replies, except for a subagent's approval request, which needs buttons: the binding refuses it and the session withdraws it.

Providers.<name>.Endpoint.default: `""` (the provider type supplies its own default URL)
Providers.<name>.Endpoint.description: Base URL of the provider API.

Providers.<name>.AuthMethod.description: How netclaw authenticates to the provider.

Providers.<name>.ApiKey.description: API key. Lives in `secrets.json`: `netclaw secrets set Providers.<name>.ApiKey <key>`.

Providers.<name>.VendorOptions.description: Provider-specific non-secret options, for example `GitHubHost` and `GitHubApiBase` for `github-copilot`, `ThinkingDialect` for `openai-compatible`, `DisableThinking` for `ollama`, `ExcludeReasoning` for `openrouter` and `IncludeVeniceSystemPrompt` for `veniceai`. Each provider type defines its own keys.

Providers.<name>.description: One provider connection. The name is yours to choose and `Models.Definitions` entries refer to it.

Providers.<name>.OAuthAccessToken.description: OAuth access token. netclaw writes it to `secrets.json` when you sign in with an OAuth auth method.

Providers.<name>.OAuthRefreshToken.description: OAuth refresh token. netclaw writes it to `secrets.json` when you sign in with an OAuth auth method.

Providers.<name>.OAuthAccountId.description: OAuth account identifier. netclaw writes it to `secrets.json` when you sign in with an OAuth auth method.

Providers.<name>.OAuthTokenExpiry.description: Expiry time of the OAuth access token, ISO 8601. netclaw writes it to `secrets.json` beside the tokens when you sign in with an OAuth auth method. It is the one value there that isn't encrypted. A key left in `netclaw.json` is retired: `netclaw doctor` reports it and `netclaw doctor --fix` moves it, after a backup.

Session.Tuning.MaxToolDescriptionChars.description: Longest MCP tool description kept at registration. Longer ones are truncated to protect the context window. `0` turns truncation off.

Session.Tuning.MaxToolSchemaWarnChars.description: Size of an MCP tool's JSON schema that triggers a warning in the log. The schema itself is never truncated, so this only reports bloated tool definitions. `0` turns the warning off.

Retention.Logs.Days.description: Days to keep `daemon-yyyy-MM-dd.log`, its numbered segments `daemon-yyyy-MM-dd.N.log` (the daemon starts a new segment at 10 MiB) and `crash-*.log` files in the logs directory. The daemon deletes older files 30 seconds after it starts and every 12 hours after that. The newest 3 daemon logs, segments counted as files, and the newest 3 crash logs are always kept. `0` keeps them forever. Per-session logs are never touched. See [Data retention](/configuration/data-retention/).

McpServers.<server>.OAuthClientSecret.description: Client secret for a pre-registered confidential OAuth client. Vault only: the schema rejects it in `netclaw.json`, so doctor fails the Config Schema check. Set it with `netclaw mcp add --client-id <id> --client-secret <secret>` or `netclaw secrets set`, which store it in `secrets.json`. Needs `OAuthClientId`.

Slack.BotToken.description: Bot token, `xoxb-`. Lives in `secrets.json`: `netclaw secrets set Slack.BotToken <token>`.

Slack.AppToken.description: App-level token, `xapp-`, for Socket Mode. Lives in `secrets.json`.

Discord.BotToken.description: Bot token. Lives in `secrets.json`: `netclaw secrets set Discord.BotToken <token>`.

Mattermost.BotToken.description: Bot access token. Lives in `secrets.json`: `netclaw secrets set Mattermost.BotToken <token>`.

Providers.<name>.VendorOptions.ThinkingD.description: `openai-compatible` only. How netclaw sends a thinking level to the server. Without it only the output limit works. `netclaw model set` saves `ReasoningEffort` when it detects llama.cpp. Set it by hand for vLLM, SGLang or a proxy.

Slack.summary: The Slack adapter. [Set up Slack](/channels/slack/) walks through the app manifest and tokens.

Discord.summary: The Discord adapter. [Set up Discord](/channels/discord/) covers the bot, intents and tokens.

Mattermost.summary: The Mattermost adapter. [Set up Mattermost](/channels/mattermost/) covers the bot account and callback URL.

Logging.summary: Daemon log level and console output. Logs go to `daemon-<date>.log` under the data directory regardless of these keys, rolling into numbered segments at 10 MiB.

Telemetry.summary: OpenTelemetry export. [OpenTelemetry](/observability/opentelemetry/) shows how to wire a collector.

Session.summary: Per-conversation timeouts, compaction and memory-capture timing. The timeout keys take whole seconds, `IdleTimeout` takes `HH:mm:ss`. [Sessions](/architecture/sessions/) explains the lifecycle these keys tune.
Session.notes: A value below a key's minimum fails `netclaw doctor` schema validation. The daemon itself enforces a 1 second minimum on `TurnLlmTimeoutSeconds`, `ToolExecutionTimeoutSeconds` and `SidecarLlmTimeoutSeconds`.

Security.summary: Deployment posture and shell mode, which choose the default tool profiles. [Security model](/security/security-model/) explains the three postures.

Tools.summary: Tool grants per audience, file roots, approval policy and `web_fetch` limits. A configured list replaces the default list, so a list with one tool grants one tool. [Built-in tools](/reference/tools/) lists the tools and defaults, and [How tool approvals work](/security/approvals/) covers `ApprovalPolicy`.

Providers.summary: Where each model is served. [Managed providers](/configuration/managed-providers/) and [self-hosted providers](/configuration/self-hosted-providers/) have one example per provider type.

Models.summary: Which model plays Main, Fallback and Compaction, and each definition's context window, modalities, output limit and thinking level. [Model configuration](/configuration/models/) has examples. The older inline shape (`Models.Main`, `Models.Fallback`, `Models.Compaction` as objects) still loads. Mixing it with `Definitions` and `Roles` stops startup.

Memory.summary: Cross-session memory, embeddings and recall. [Memory and embeddings](/configuration/memory/) explains how the pieces fit together. The embedding model downloads on first start unless `Embeddings.AutoDownload` is `false`.
Memory.notes: Set `Memory.Enabled` to `false` and the memory tools and automatic recall disappear for every audience.

Search.summary: The `web_search` backend. [Search providers](/configuration/search-providers/) covers Brave and SearXNG setup.

SkillSync.summary: Switch for the skill index tools. [Skills overview](/skills/overview/) explains where skills come from.

ExternalSkills.summary: Skill directories from other tools, such as Claude Code. [External skills](/skills/external-skills/) has the setup.

SkillFeeds.summary: Private skill servers that netclaw syncs from at startup and on a timer. [Skill feeds](/skills/skill-feeds/) has the setup.

SubAgents.summary: Switches and watchdogs for `spawn_agent`. [Custom subagents](/skills/custom-subagents/) shows how to define agents.

Notifications.summary: Where operational alerts go. [Operational alerts](/observability/operational-alerts/) lists the alert types.

Webhooks.summary: The inbound webhook endpoint. The routes themselves aren't in `netclaw.json`: each one is a file under `config/webhooks/`, managed with `netclaw webhooks` or the webhook tools. [Webhooks](/configuration/webhooks/) covers routes and verification.

Scheduling.summary: Switch for reminders and scheduled tasks. [Reminders](/configuration/reminders/) covers creating and running them.
Scheduling.notes: Set `Scheduling.Enabled` to `false` and the five reminder tools aren't registered.

Daemon.summary: Bind address, port and how the daemon is exposed to the network. Changing any of these in `netclaw.json` restarts the daemon. [Exposure modes](/deployment/exposure-modes/) explains each mode and [Docker](/deployment/docker/) covers the container settings.
Daemon.notes:
The Docker image's health check probes port 5199. A container with a different `Daemon.Port` reports `unhealthy` even though the daemon is up, so override the health check when you change the port.

In `Local` exposure mode the daemon answers 401 to a request whose `Host` isn't `localhost` or a loopback IP literal (`127.0.0.1`, `[::1]`), or whose `Origin`, when present, isn't `http://` plus the same host. A client that reaches the daemon by another host name, or a browser app on another port, is refused. `Daemon.Host` as a bind value still accepts spellings such as `127.1`.

Workspaces.summary: Where netclaw looks for your project repositories. [Context structure](/architecture/context-structure/) explains how projects feed the prompt.

McpServers.summary: MCP server profiles keyed by name. Add them with `netclaw mcp add` or edit the file. [MCP servers](/configuration/mcp-servers/) has the walkthrough and [MCP tool permissions](/guides/mcp-tool-permissions/) covers per-audience access.

Retention.summary: How long the daemon keeps log files before a scheduled clean-up deletes them. [Data retention](/configuration/data-retention/) explains what is and isn't deleted.
